name: Wall Serving
description:
1. Stand 10-15 feet from a wall.
2. Practice your underhand or overhand serve into the wall.
3. Focus on contacting the ball with a flat hand and following through.
4. Catch the rebound and repeat.
5. Do 3 sets of 10 serves, alternating between underhand and overhand.

name: Target Serving
description:
1. Place cones or towels in different zones on the opposite court.
2. Serve from behind the end line aiming at a specific target.
3. Score points for hitting each zone (center = 1 pt, corners = 3 pts).
4. Each player gets 10 serves per round.
5. Rotate targets after each round to work on accuracy and placement.

name: Serving Relay Race
description:
1. Split into two teams lined up behind the end line.
2. First player serves over the net.
3. If the serve goes over and lands in, they run to the back of the line.
4. If they miss, they must serve again until successful.
5. First team to have all players complete a good serve wins.

name: Serving Zones
description:
1. Divide the opposite court into 6 zones (1-6).
2. Coach calls out a zone number.
3. Player must serve into that zone.
4. Successful serves earn a point; track individual scores.
5. Play 3 rounds of 6 serves each.
6. Emphasize consistent toss and follow-through.

name: Progressive Serving
description:
1. Start serving from the 10-foot line.
2. After 3 successful serves in a row, take two steps back.
3. Continue moving back toward the end line with each set of 3.
4. If you miss, stay at that distance and try again.
5. Goal: successfully serve from behind the end line.
6. Great for building confidence in younger players.

name: Serve & Chase
description:
1. Player serves over the net.
2. Immediately sprint under the net to the other side.
3. Field your own serve with a pass to a target.
4. Jog back and repeat.
5. Builds serving accuracy plus transition footwork.
6. Do 8-10 reps per player.

name: Over The Net
description:
1. Line up players on the service line, each with a ball.
2. Players practice serving the ball over the net repeatedly.
3. Coach watches technique and offers individual assistance.
4. Emphasize that getting the serve over is more important than power.
5. Show proper technique for both overhand and underhand serves.
6. Repetition is key — run this drill at every practice.

name: Serving Tape
description:
1. String a tape line from antenna to antenna, about 3 feet above the top of the net.
2. Players line up on the service line.
3. Serve the ball overhand so it passes between the net tape and the upper tape line.
4. Serving over the upper tape or into the net = 2 finger-tip push-ups.
5. Focus on a flat, controlled trajectory.
6. Builds low, consistent overhand serves that are hard to return.

name: Miss The Chairs
description:
1. Set up 3 chairs in the back court where serve receivers would stand.
2. Put a tape circle (2-foot radius) around each chair.
3. Players serve from behind the end line.
4. Objective: serve into the lanes between the chairs, NOT hitting any chair or circle.
5. Hitting a chair or circle = 2 finger-tip push-ups.
6. Teaches players to serve to the gaps and weak spots of a defense.

name: Target Service Drill
description:
1. Place 3 targets on the opposite court: back left, back right, and short center.
2. Servers line up in groups of 6 on the service line.
3. Each server gets 10 serves to hit all 3 targets.
4. Each missed target = 1 set of lines; ball not over net = 2 sets.
5. Focus on good contact, trajectory, toss, and follow-through.
6. Builds serving accuracy and consistency under pressure.

name: Pepper
description:
1. Pair up with a partner about 10 feet apart.
2. Player A hits (downball) to Player B.
3. Player B passes (bumps) back to Player A.
4. Player A sets to Player B.
5. Player B hits back to Player A.
6. Repeat the sequence: hit-pass-set-hit.
7. Focus on controlled contacts and proper platform angle.

name: Partner Passing
description:
1. Two players face each other about 15 feet apart.
2. One player tosses or serves the ball.
3. Receiving player passes it back using a forearm bump.
4. Focus on: feet shoulder-width, knees bent, arms together, angle the platform.
5. Do 20 passes then switch roles.
6. Count consecutive good passes as a team challenge.

name: Passing Triangle
description:
1. Three players form a triangle about 12 feet apart.
2. Ball is passed (bumped) around the triangle in order.
3. After each pass, the passer shuffles one position clockwise.
4. Maintain a controlled, arcing pass.
5. Challenge: keep the ball going for 30 consecutive passes.
6. Rotate direction after each set.

name: Shuttle Passing
description:
1. Two lines face each other across the net (or 15 feet apart).
2. Front player in Line A tosses the ball to front player in Line B.
3. Line B player passes it back, then runs to the back of Line A.
4. Line A catches and tosses to the next Line B player.
5. Continue rotating through for 5 minutes.
6. Focus on moving feet to the ball before passing.

name: Queen/King of the Court Passing
description:
1. Teams of 2 on each side of the net.
2. Coach initiates play with a toss or serve.
3. Receiving team must pass, set, and send the ball over.
4. Winning team stays and rotates to the 'King' side.
5. Losing team goes to the end of the challenger line.
6. First team to win 5 rallies on the King side wins.

name: Table Top
description:
1. Pair up players and give each pair a ball.
2. Teach proper forearm passing form: create a flat 'table top' surface with forearms.
3. Stand with one foot in front of the other, knees bent.
4. Lift through the ball using your legs, not your arms.
5. Partners practice controlled passing back and forth.
6. Focus on keeping the platform flat and steady with every pass.

name: Moving Table Top
description:
1. Form two lines with a coach at each station.
2. Coach tosses the ball to the left or right at varying heights.
3. Player shuffles to get into position underneath the ball.
4. Execute a proper forearm pass back to the coach.
5. Focus on moving feet first, then setting the platform.
6. Builds on basic Table Top by adding lateral movement.

name: Continuous Passing
description:
1. Pair up players of similar skill and give them a ball.
2. One player tosses the ball to start.
3. Coach calls out the type of pass: high pass, flat low pass, or self-pass then partner pass.
4. Players execute the called pass type continuously.
5. Progress to calling set types (face passes) as well.
6. Builds controlled passing in a variety of scenarios.

name: Pipeline Passing
description:
1. Make two tape lines down the middle of the court, 12 feet apart.
2. Two players pass inside this area starting in the middle.
3. After each pass, shuffle right, touch the tape line, return to center.
4. Partner passes back while you are moving.
5. Goal: 10 consecutive passes (5 each) without dropping.
6. Builds lateral movement, conditioning, and passing under fatigue.

name: Harass The Passer
description:
1. Set up 2-3 servers on one side with a target player at the net.
2. Two passers split the court, each with a 'harasser' in their back pocket.
3. Servers serve the ball to the passers.
4. The harasser yells, screams, stomps, and feints — but never touches the passer.
5. Passer must stay focused and pass accurately to the target.
6. Builds concentration and ability to ignore distractions during play.

name: Reaction Passing
description:
1. Set up 2-3 servers on each side with a line of passers.
2. Passer stands with their back to the server.
3. Coach blows the whistle — server serves the ball.
4. Once the passer hears the ball being struck, they turn around.
5. Passer must quickly locate the ball and make a good pass.
6. Simulates quick defensive reaction against fast attacks.

name: Setting to the Wall
description:
1. Stand 3 feet from a wall.
2. Set the ball against the wall continuously.
3. Use proper hand shape: fingers spread, thumbs and forefingers forming a triangle.
4. Push through with legs and wrists.
5. Do 3 sets of 30 wall sets.
6. Step back to 5 feet for the next round to work on power.

name: Setting to Self
description:
1. Stand in athletic position with knees slightly bent.
2. Set the ball straight up above your forehead.
3. Catch it in the proper setting position, then set again.
4. Progress to continuous sets without catching.
5. Goal: 50 consecutive self-sets without losing control.
6. Keep the ball spinning backward with proper wrist action.

name: Partner Setting
description:
1. Two players face each other 10-12 feet apart.
2. Player A tosses high to Player B.
3. Player B sets it back to Player A's hands.
4. Focus on clean hand contact, pushing evenly with both hands.
5. After 20 good sets, switch roles.
6. Progress by increasing distance to 20 feet.

name: Setting Target Practice
description:
1. Set up a hula hoop or cone at the left and right antenna positions.
2. Player receives a toss from a coach near the net.
3. Set the ball to land in the target area.
4. Alternate between setting to the left and right pins.
5. Score: 2 points for hoop, 1 point for within 3 feet.
6. First to 20 points wins.

name: Setting Footwork Drill
description:
1. Setter starts at the net in position 2/3.
2. Coach tosses the ball to different spots along the net.
3. Setter must shuffle to the ball, square up, and set to the outside.
4. After setting, shuffle back to starting position.
5. Repeat 10 times to the left, 10 times to the right.
6. Emphasize arriving before the ball and being balanced.

name: Set and Follow
description:
1. Put players in groups of three with one ball.
2. Two players on one side, one on the other.
3. A player from the two-side tosses to the single player.
4. Single player sets it back, then follows their set to that side.
5. The tosser follows their toss to the single side.
6. Continue continuously — builds setting skills, footwork, and keeping your head up.

name: Walking Setters
description:
1. Clear the court for setters (or all players).
2. Start in one corner. Set the ball while walking forward across the court.
3. At the other side, move over 10 feet along the sideline.
4. Walk backward while maintaining controlled sets.
5. Then shuffle sideways across the court while setting.
6. Builds ball control, concentration, and coordination while moving.

name: Around The World Setting
description:
1. Set up one line of players outside the court between the back and attack line.
2. Three tossers on each side of the net.
3. Player enters and receives a bump from tosser 1, shuffles to tosser 2 for a set, then tosser 3 for a bump.
4. Repeat the sequence on the other side of the net.
5. Dotted lines = passes back to tossers; solid lines = player movement.
6. Works passing, setting, and footwork. Pick up pace for conditioning.

name: Approach and Hit
description:
1. Start behind the 10-foot line on the left side.
2. Practice the 3-step approach: left-right-left (for right-handers).
3. On the last two steps, plant and jump.
4. Coach or partner tosses a high ball near the net.
5. Swing and contact the ball at the highest point.
6. Land on both feet. Repeat 10 times each side.

name: Hitting Lines
description:
1. Form a hitting line behind the 10-foot line on the left pin.
2. Setter at the net receives a pass from a tosser.
3. Setter delivers a high outside set.
4. Hitter approaches, jumps, and hits cross-court or down the line.
5. Shagger retrieves the ball.
6. Rotate through 10 hits per player. Switch to right side.

name: Toss-Hit-Catch
description:
1. Pair up. One player at the net, one at the 10-foot line.
2. Net player tosses high to the approaching hitter.
3. Hitter uses full approach and spikes.
4. Focus on arm swing: elbow high, snap the wrist, follow through.
5. After 10 hits, switch roles.
6. Great for beginners learning timing.

name: Target Hitting
description:
1. Place cones or towels in zones on the opposite court.
2. Setter sets from position 2/3.
3. Hitter approaches and aims at a specific target zone.
4. Score points based on accuracy (zone 1=1pt, zone 5=3pts, etc.).
5. Each hitter gets 8 attempts.
6. Track scores and declare a winner.

name: Standing Spike Drill
description:
1. Player stands on a box or platform at the net.
2. Coach holds or tosses the ball just above net height.
3. Player practices arm swing and wrist snap from a standing position.
4. Focus on hand on top of the ball, snapping down.
5. Do 15 reps, then step off the box and practice with a jump.
6. Builds proper contact point without worrying about timing.

name: Snap The Wrist
description:
1. Each player gets a ball and stands 10-15 feet from a wall.
2. Toss the ball up and hit it using proper reach-back, strike, and follow-through.
3. The ball should land on the floor a couple feet before the wall, bounce up and deflect back.
4. Repeat continuously — if it hits the wall first, you need more wrist snap.
5. If it goes straight down, ease up on the snap.
6. Teaches the proper wrist snap that sends the ball sharply downward.

name: Tennis Ball Throw
description:
1. Set up several stations across the net for attackers.
2. Player starts at the attack line with a tennis ball.
3. Coach hands them the ball as they begin their 3-step approach.
4. At the top of the jump, throw the tennis ball using hitting motion.
5. Bring the ball back, keep elbow high, snap wrist, and drive it down.
6. Pick a spot to aim at — simulates a real spike without worrying about contact.

name: 10 Hits Drill
description:
1. Include a passer and setter on each side of the net.
2. Divide remaining players into two hitting groups.
3. Coach tosses to the passer, who passes to the setter, who sets for the hitter.
4. Each hitter must complete 10 successful hits (no net tape, ball in court).
5. No more than 3 tips allowed — the rest must be full hits.
6. Last person to finish does an extra set of lines. Great for repetition.

name: Corner Tip Drill
description:
1. Place baskets (clothes baskets) inside the attack line on both sides of each court half.
2. Attackers line up in two groups on either side of the net.
3. Coach tosses balls up at the net for the attackers.
4. Hitters decide whether to tip to the near or far basket.
5. Ball in basket = 1 point. Most points at the end wins.
6. Add a blocker to make it more game-like — hitter reads the block to decide where to tip.

name: Hourglass Attack
description:
1. Tape an hourglass shape on the court (narrow in middle, wide at ends).
2. Divide into four 3-player teams: power hitter, offside hitter, middle hitter.
3. Power and offside hitters each hit 3 times: sideline, cross-court, and deep middle.
4. Middle hitters hit sharp right and sharp left to sidelines.
5. Hits landing outside the hourglass = +1 point; inside = -1 point.
6. Winning team runs one fewer set of lines. Builds accuracy under pressure.

name: Find The Hole
description:
1. Set up a defense in a standard formation on one side.
2. Attackers on the other side run a normal 3-hit offense.
3. Hitters must read the block position and defensive alignment.
4. Hit the ball to open areas where defenders are NOT positioned.
5. Switch defensive formations to increase difficulty.
6. Teaches hitters to read defenses in real time and place shots smartly.

name: Defensive Shuffle Drill
description:
1. Player starts in defensive position at the back row.
2. Coach stands at the net and hits or tosses balls to the left and right.
3. Player shuffles laterally and digs each ball up to a target.
4. Reset to center after each dig.
5. Do 3 sets of 10 digs.
6. Focus on staying low, reading the hitter, and platform control.

name: Dig and Roll
description:
1. Player starts in ready position in the back court.
2. Coach tips or hits a ball just out of comfortable reach.
3. Player extends to dig the ball up, then performs a controlled roll.
4. Get up quickly and return to ready position.
5. Repeat 10 times to each side.
6. Teaches players to safely extend their range.

name: Rapid Fire Defense
description:
1. One player in the back row in defensive stance.
2. Three coaches/players at the net with volleyballs.
3. They take turns hitting or tipping balls at the defender.
4. Defender must dig each ball up as quickly as possible.
5. Go for 30 seconds, then switch defenders.
6. Builds reaction time and reading multiple attackers.

name: Pancake Drill
description:
1. Players partner up. One lies on their stomach.
2. Coach yells 'Go!' — player jumps up to ready position.
3. Partner immediately tosses a low ball.
4. Player dives forward and uses a pancake (flat hand on floor) to save it.
5. Alternate after 5 reps.
6. Teaches the emergency pancake dig technique.

name: Down Ball Defense
description:
1. Three back-row defenders in positions 1, 5, and 6.
2. Coach or player at the net hits controlled down balls.
3. Defenders read the hit and pass (dig) to the setter target.
4. Setter catches and returns the ball to the coach.
5. Rotate positions after every 5 balls.
6. Emphasize reading the attacker's shoulder and arm angle.

name: Toss and Dig
description:
1. Pair up with a partner about 10 feet apart.
2. Partner tosses the ball underhand at waist-to-knee level.
3. Receiving player gets into defensive stance and digs the ball up.
4. Focus on: knees bent, weight forward, arms together, angle platform up.
5. Do 15 reps then switch roles.
6. Great introduction to the digging motion for new players.

name: Dig Drill
description:
1. Coach hits balls at players with moderate power.
2. Set up 2 or more groups for extra repetition.
3. Players must get low and pass (dig) the ball up under control.
4. Focus on proper technique: get low, lift through, don't swing arms.
5. Absorb the ball rather than meeting it with hard contact.
6. Basic drill used as a game-time warm up by many teams.

name: Dig and Dash
description:
1. Coach at the net, two lines of players in each back corner.
2. Coach hits a ball down to one line — player digs it back up.
3. Player immediately sprints to the other side of the net.
4. Coach flips a tip ball — player must field the tip.
5. After tip, player goes to the shagging line; shagger joins a dig line.
6. Builds quickness, proper dig form, and transition footwork.

name: Net Save Drill
description:
1. Coach stands at mid-court with balls. Two lines on either side of the attack line.
2. Coach throws the ball against the net to simulate a net ball.
3. Player watches where the ball will come off the net.
4. Important: watch the ball hit the net before moving — don't guess!
5. Get underneath the ball and make a controlled pass to a teammate.
6. Teaches proper reaction to unpredictable net rebounds.

name: Turn And Dig
description:
1. Set up 4 stations with a player at the net and a group at the back court.
2. Player at the service line stands with their back to the net.
3. Net player slaps the ball — back player turns around.
4. Net player tips or tosses the ball to a random spot.
5. Back player must locate and dig the ball successfully.
6. 10 successful digs to finish. Builds reaction and awareness.

name: Sit And Recover
description:
1. Six players in normal defensive positions — but sitting on the floor, backs to the coach.
2. Coach at the net calls 'UP!' — all players jump to their feet.
3. Coach immediately tips, hits, or tosses the ball to an area.
4. Players must read where the ball is going and execute a dig.
5. Progress from 1-hit recovery to full 3-hit plays.
6. Develops read-and-react skills and quick recovery from disadvantage.

name: Mirror Blocking
description:
1. Two players face each other on opposite sides of the net.
2. One is the attacker (slides left and right along the net).
3. The blocker mirrors the attacker's movement using shuffle steps.
4. When the attacker raises their arms to 'hit', the blocker jumps and presses hands over.
5. Do 10 reps then switch roles.
6. Builds lateral movement and timing at the net.

name: Block and Transition
description:
1. Blocker starts at the net in blocking position.
2. Coach on the opposite side tosses the ball up and hits.
3. Blocker jumps and blocks, then immediately drops off the net.
4. After landing, blocker transitions to hit an approach on a set from a teammate.
5. Repeat 8 times per player.
6. Teaches the block-to-attack transition movement.

name: Footwork Blocking Drill
description:
1. Blocker starts at the middle of the net.
2. Coach calls 'Left!' or 'Right!'
3. Blocker uses crossover-step and shuffle to reach the pin.
4. Jump and press hands over the net with proper form.
5. Land and shuffle back to center.
6. Repeat 5 times each direction. Focus on: quick feet, hands above net, seal the net.

name: Solo Block Jumps
description:
1. Stand at the net in athletic position, hands at shoulder height.
2. Jump straight up, pressing both hands above the net.
3. Fingers spread wide, wrists firm, push hands toward the opposite court.
4. Land softly on both feet and immediately jump again.
5. Do 3 sets of 10 jumps.
6. Builds blocking endurance and proper hand positioning.

name: Double Block Drill
description:
1. Two blockers start at the net — one middle, one outside.
2. Coach or hitter approaches from the opposite side.
3. Middle blocker closes to the outside blocker to form a double block.
4. Both jump together, pressing hands and sealing the gap between them.
5. Repeat from the other side.
6. Do 8 reps each side. Emphasize communication ('Here! Here!') and timing.

name: Angle Your Block
description:
1. Three blockers set up in blocking positions at the net.
2. Coach stands on the opposite side and tosses balls to different spots.
3. Blockers must angle their hands so the ball deflects back into the court.
4. Toss balls to left, right, and middle — blockers adjust hand angle each time.
5. Focus on proper hand penetration over the net.
6. Teaches the fundamental concept of angling blocks inward.

name: Slide Block
description:
1. Three blockers on one side, three hitters on the other.
2. Coach stands at net facing hitters, back to blockers.
3. Coach points to which hitter will approach — blockers must react.
4. Blockers slide and shuffle together along the net to set the block.
5. Quick lateral footwork is key — watch for proper shuffle technique.
6. Teaches blockers to slide as a unit to cover the attacking position.

name: Shadow Blocking
description:
1. Pair up players of similar skill across the net — no balls.
2. Attacker approaches from the left side; blocker sets up the block.
3. Both shuffle to the middle — attacker approaches again, blocker reacts.
4. Then shuffle to the right for a third approach.
5. Switch sides after one full run-through.
6. Teaches blockers to read the attacker's body angle, approach direction, and timing.

name: Blind Blocking
description:
1. Pair players across the net. Coach tosses ball to the attacker.
2. Blocker focuses on the attacker's body — NOT the ball.
3. Read the attacker's shoulder angle, approach direction, and arm position.
4. Set up the block based on body language cues.
5. This breaks the habit of watching the ball and missing the block.
6. Add a second blocker to practice coordinated blind blocking.

name: High Knees
description:
1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
2. Drive one knee up to hip height, then quickly switch to the other.
3. Pump your arms in rhythm — opposite arm to opposite knee.
4. Stay on the balls of your feet.
5. Go for 30 seconds, rest 10 seconds, repeat 3 times.
6. Great for raising heart rate and activating hip flexors before practice.

name: Butt Kicks
description:
1. Jog in place or move forward slowly.
2. On each step, kick your heel up toward your glutes.
3. Keep your upper body upright and core engaged.
4. Pump arms naturally as you would when running.
5. Go for 30 seconds, rest 10 seconds, repeat 3 times.
6. Warms up quadriceps and hamstrings for explosive court movements.

name: Arm Circles
description:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended out to the sides.
2. Make small forward circles for 15 seconds.
3. Gradually increase to large forward circles for 15 seconds.
4. Reverse direction — small backward circles for 15 seconds, then large.
5. Finish with 10 big windmill circles (full range of motion).
6. Essential for warming up shoulders before serving, hitting, and setting.

name: Leg Swings
description:
1. Stand next to a wall or partner for balance.
2. Swing one leg forward and backward in a controlled motion, 15 times.
3. Then swing the same leg side to side across your body, 15 times.
4. Switch to the other leg and repeat both directions.
5. Keep your core tight and stand tall throughout.
6. Opens up hips and prepares legs for lateral shuffles and jumping.

name: Side Shuffles
description:
1. Start in athletic stance: knees bent, weight on balls of feet.
2. Shuffle laterally to the right for 15 feet, staying low.
3. Touch the line, then shuffle back to the left.
4. Keep feet wide — never let them cross or come together.
5. Do 5 round trips.
6. Mirrors the defensive movement pattern used throughout volleyball.

name: Carioca (Grapevine)
description:
1. Start in athletic stance facing sideways.
2. Step your trailing foot in front, then lead foot steps out.
3. Step trailing foot behind, then lead foot steps out.
4. Alternate front-behind as you move laterally.
5. Use hip rotation and arm swing for rhythm.
6. Go 15 feet, switch directions. Do 4 round trips. Builds hip mobility and coordination.

name: Walking Lunges with Twist
description:
1. Step forward into a deep lunge (front knee at 90 degrees).
2. At the bottom of the lunge, rotate your upper body toward the front knee.
3. Hold the twist for 1 second, then step forward into the next lunge.
4. Alternate legs as you move across the court.
5. Do 10 lunges per leg (20 total steps).
6. Activates glutes, quads, and core rotation used in hitting and serving.

name: Partner Ball Throw Warmup
description:
1. Pair up with a partner, 10-15 feet apart, each with a volleyball.
2. Throw the ball back and forth using two-hand overhead throws.
3. After 10 reps, switch to one-hand throws (mimicking serving motion).
4. Then do 10 underhand tosses focusing on accuracy.
5. Finish with 10 bounce-catch throws to work on reaction.
6. Activates shoulders and gets players comfortable handling the ball.

name: Setting Warmup
description:
1. Each player gets a ball.
2. Set the ball to yourself continuously, staying in one spot — 20 reps.
3. Then walk forward while setting to yourself — across the court.
4. Walk backward while setting — return to start.
5. Partner up: face-to-face setting, 20 controlled sets each.
6. Finish with 10 quick sets each. Gradually increases intensity for setting muscles.

name: Pepper Warmup
description:
1. Pair up with a partner about 10 feet apart.
2. Start at half speed: bump-set-hit, bump-set-hit sequence.
3. Focus on clean contacts — control over power.
4. After 2 minutes, increase to three-quarter speed.
5. After another 2 minutes, go full speed.
6. Classic warmup that touches all three core contacts before practice begins.

name: Inchworms
description:
1. Stand tall with feet together.
2. Bend at the waist and place hands on the floor in front of you.
3. Walk your hands forward into a plank/push-up position.
4. Hold the plank for 2 seconds.
5. Walk your feet up toward your hands, keeping legs as straight as possible.
6. Stand up and repeat across the court. Stretches hamstrings and activates core and shoulders.

name: Lateral Band Walks
description:
1. Place a resistance band around both ankles (or just above knees).
2. Get into a half-squat athletic stance.
3. Step sideways, leading with one foot, keeping tension on the band.
4. Take 15 steps to the right, then 15 steps back to the left.
5. Stay low the entire time — don't bounce up.
6. Fires up glutes and hip stabilizers critical for lateral court movement.

name: A-Skip and B-Skip
description:
1. A-Skip: skip forward driving one knee up to hip height on each skip.
2. Pump opposite arm up with each knee drive.
3. Go across the court and back (about 30 feet each way).
4. B-Skip: same motion but extend the leg forward at the top before pulling it down.
5. Emphasize quick ground contact and tall posture.
6. Activates hip flexors, calves, and coordination for explosive jumping.

name: Volleyball Jog and Pass
description:
1. Players jog in pairs around the court perimeter.
2. While jogging, bump-pass a volleyball back and forth between partners.
3. Maintain controlled passes while on the move — don't stop jogging.
4. After 2 laps, switch to overhead sets while jogging.
5. After 2 more laps, alternate between bumps and sets each contact.
6. Combines cardio warmup with ball-handling to save time.

name: Serve Receive Warmup
description:
1. One player serves easy balls from the service line.
2. Three receivers spread out in a W formation on the other side.
3. Start at half speed — serve underhand with placement.
4. Receivers pass to a target player at the net.
5. After 10 serves, increase to three-quarter speed overhand serves.
6. Finish with 10 full-speed serves. Gradually builds to game-like intensity.

name: Shoulder Band Warmup
description:
1. Hold a resistance band with both hands, shoulder-width apart.
2. Pull the band apart with straight arms — 15 reps.
3. Then hold the band overhead and pull apart — 15 reps.
4. Internal rotation: elbow at 90°, rotate forearm inward against band — 15 per arm.
5. External rotation: elbow at 90°, rotate forearm outward — 15 per arm.
6. Prevents shoulder injuries from repetitive serving and hitting.
